zh-CN.Examine bonding surfaces, nominal stress: Examine bonding surfaces, nominal stress, and controlled specimen comparisons without confusing a higher failure force with an intrinsic adhesive property.
zh-CN.A Stronger Pull Is Not Yet an Explanatio: A Stronger Pull Is Not Yet an Explanation
zh-CN.A demonstration can show one joint carry: A demonstration can show one joint carrying a larger force than another without identifying why. Frihart and Hunt's Wood Handbook Chapter 10 [1] explains wood adhesion, surface properties, the bonding process, and performance testing. This article uses that research context to propose an interpretable surface-preparation comparison. It introduces no measured joint strengths and ranks no adhesives. The central question is whether an observed difference can reasonably be attributed to surface preparation after specimen geometry, wood variation, application, assembly, and conditioning have been considered.
zh-CN.The handbook describes adhesion as depen: The handbook describes adhesion as depending on the wood surface, adhesive, and bonding process rather than on a product name alone. Its surface and bonding discussions address wetting, surface condition, and preparation, while its performance discussion considers joint testing. These mechanisms justify recording preparation and process history. They do not establish one universally best abrasive grit or a preparation recipe for every wood and adhesive. A real procedure must follow the particular adhesive system's requirements and the intended joint. Keep the supported mechanism separate from any new comparison being proposed.
zh-CN.A treatment called sanded is too broad t: A treatment called sanded is too broad to reproduce. A proposed study should specify the wood surface, abrasive sequence, tool, direction, dust-removal method, elapsed time before bonding, and storage conditions. A planed treatment likewise needs its machining procedure recorded. If one group is freshly machined and the other is several days old, surface age is another variable. Either control it or make it an explicit experimental factor. Record actual observations of damage or contamination rather than assuming preparation labels describe identical surfaces across every specimen.
zh-CN.Use Geometry to Expose a Ranking Trap: Use Geometry to Expose a Ranking Trap
zh-CN.Consider two invented joint tests. Speci: Consider two invented joint tests. Specimen A has a nominal bonded area of 20 × 100 = 2000 mm² and fails at 5000 N, giving an apparent nominal stress of 2.50 N/mm². Specimen B has a 25 × 100 = 2500 mm² area and fails at 5500 N, giving 2.20 N/mm². B carries a larger force, while A has a larger force divided by nominal area. Neither ranking alone establishes an intrinsic adhesive strength. The numbers were chosen solely to demonstrate how changing geometry changes the question answered by a test result.
zh-CN.Nominal Stress Is Not a Uniform Local Fi: Nominal Stress Is Not a Uniform Local Field
zh-CN.Dividing force by nominal area is useful: Dividing force by nominal area is useful bookkeeping, but it does not show that stress was uniform across the joint. Eccentric loading, grip arrangement, joint stiffness, and specimen geometry may introduce uneven shear or peel. The comparison should therefore use a suitable, documented test method with comparable specimens rather than inventing a general strength property from a pull demonstration. Preserve the method's definition of the reported quantity. If a coupon study is meant to inform an actual assembly, explain which aspects of that assembly the coupon represents and which it leaves out.
zh-CN.Prepare several independent matched sets: Prepare several independent matched sets from identified boards, retaining species, moisture condition, grain orientation, and a specimen map. Randomly assign the preparation treatments within each set where feasible. Hold adhesive identification, spread procedure, joint dimensions, assembly interval, pressure procedure, cure, and test conditions consistent with the selected method. Record departures rather than silently repeating an unsuccessful specimen until it produces a preferred result. Multiple coupons from one board are useful, but their shared origin limits what they establish about variation between boards. Report both the board count and the coupon count.
zh-CN.A failed specimen may separate in the ad: A failed specimen may separate in the adhesive region, at an interface, in the wood, or through a mixed pattern. Photograph and classify the failure using the selected method's definitions. A high proportion of wood failure can be relevant evidence, but it does not by itself prove that the joint meets every service requirement. Likewise, a surface treatment that changes failure location may deserve investigation even when the average force changes little. Keep force, apparent nominal stress, failure description, and specimen history together so an interpretation is not based on the largest number alone.
zh-CN.Transfer Only the Conclusion the Study S: Transfer Only the Conclusion the Study Supports
zh-CN.A controlled result can support a statem: A controlled result can support a statement about identified materials, preparation, geometry, conditioning, and a stated test. It cannot automatically rank all adhesives, certify long-term durability, or approve a load-bearing assembly. A practical workshop record should carry the preparation instruction beside the glue-up schedule and part labels, especially when later machining changes the bonding face. The companion assembly-window article examines timing as a separate process variable. Taken together, these records allow a joint problem to be investigated through observable conditions rather than assigning every outcome to glue choice.
zh-CN.Specify preparation, cleaning, and time: Specify preparation, cleaning, and time before bonding.
zh-CN.Match wood, joint dimensions, and bondin: Match wood, joint dimensions, and bonding process.
zh-CN.Use a documented test method and consist: Use a documented test method and consistent conditioning.
zh-CN.Report force, nominal area, and failure: Report force, nominal area, and failure location.
zh-CN.Limit conclusions to the tested material: Limit conclusions to the tested materials and procedure.
zh-CN.What must be controlled before a bond te: What must be controlled before a bond test can support a claim about surface preparation?
Surface condition is only one variable. Geometry, wood, adhesive process, conditioning, and failure mode must remain traceable.
